newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM Erbakan to see president, likely to quit.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM Erbakan to see president, likely to quit.

text.p: Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, said he would meet President Suleyman Demirel later on Wednesday, apparently to submit his resignation under a power-sharing deal with his pro-Western coalition partners.

"I will take the agreement which we have reached to the president," Erbakan said after a meeting with government ally Tansu Ciller and a far-right leader. He said he would meet Demirel at the presidential palace 6.30 p.m. (1530 GMT).

A spokesman for the Islamists told Reuters earlier Erbakan was expected to hand in his resignation during his visit to the president. But Erbakan made no direct reference to resigning during the news conference.

Ciller, the deputy prime minister, told reporters at a joint news conference with Erbakan that the year-old government would "shortly" come to an end. The coalition has been unravelling for months under pressure from the anti-Islamist military.
Erbakan had previously agreed to step down and hand over power to U.S.-educated Ciller, who would head a caretaker government to take the country to early polls.

Defections among MPs and ministers from Ciller's secularist True Path Party have robbed the coalition of a majority in the 550-seat parliament. Two MPs resigned from Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party on Wednesday, further weakening the government.
The national assembly must approve any transfer of power and early polls, and the prospects for power swap remain uncertain.
However, a far-right powerbroker has said he would back government efforts to push the coalition's plans through parliament.
